label: Support Fins
hint: Red faces need support. Turn the part with the rings (it stays on the bed); Support Fins puts breakaway fins and a bed pad under the red.

fields.label: Add as
fields.help: Part of the body: the fins are joined to it, so it exports and slices as one object (what Support Fins itself does). Separate body: a body of its own you can hide or remove; export both together.

fields.label: On the part
fields.help: Rotate: drag the rings to turn the part the way it will print (it stays on the bed, and the fins follow). Add fins: draw walls by hand where Auto left a gap. Remove fins: click a fin to take it away, click it again to bring it back.

fields.label: Placement mode
fields.help: Auto: a tined wall under each overhang steep and flat enough to grip, a plain breakaway wall under the shallow ones. Full coverage: Auto, then walls under every overhang Auto left bare -- more walls and plastic, every reachable overhang held. Wide roofs and flat shelves usually need Full coverage.

fields.label: Overhang
fields.help: Surface angle from the plate below which a face needs support.

fields.label: Nozzle
fields.help: Your printer's nozzle diameter. Sizes support walls, contact tips and tines using the website's nozzle scaling. Set it to the nozzle used to print the fins; layer height and support gap are separate settings. Default 0.4mm.

fields.label: Tines
fields.help: Tines fuse the support to the part so it grips instead of just propping. Off = plain breakaway wall.

fields.label: Tine grip
fields.help: How tightly to space the grip tines. Light = fewest marks (default), a per-wall floor keeps grip; Firm = dense comb / max grip for a tippy or tall part.

fields.label: Direction
fields.help: Horizontal: one-layer tines that grip the part and snap off clean (FDM). Vertical: pins that stand up from each wall into the part, like a resin slicer's contact tips, for resin printers, where every support has to be attached.

fields.label: Pin depth
fields.help: How far each pin sinks into the part, like a resin slicer's contact depth. Resin slicers sink a tip 0-0.2 mm; deeper leaves a bigger mark and is harder to snap off. Default 0.1 mm.

fields.label: Layer height
fields.help: Set this to the layer height you slice at. The grip tines are one layer tall so they snap off clean; if this doesn't match your slicer, the tines tear and leave marks. Default 0.2mm.

fields.label: Support gap
fields.help: Clearance between a support top and the part. Bigger = cleaner surface / easier removal; too big stops holding the overhang. Default 0.2mm.

fields.label: Bed pad
fields.help: A tilted part rests on an edge and peels off the plate without a pad. Auto: Light, or Sure hold when the part meets the plate on a point or a small round foot. Light: one layer, 0.12mm off the part, peels off like a brim. Sure hold: thicker and tacked into the part, holds harder but is harder to remove.

fields.label: Sway braces
fields.help: Stand tapered buttress ribs against the upright sides of a tall part, tied on with tines all the way up, so it doesn't drift or wobble as it grows.

fields.label: Brace grip from
fields.help: Height the brace tines start at. 0 = grip the whole height; raise it to tie on only above where the part starts to move.

fields.label: Brace tine spacing
fields.help: Vertical distance between brace tines. Smaller = held tighter, more marks on the side. Default 6mm.

fields.label: Brace depth
fields.help: How far the brace reaches out at the bed, as a share of its height. Deeper = stiffer, more plastic. Default 15%.

fields.label: Cutouts
fields.help: Cut holes through tall breakaway walls to save filament. The top edge that holds the part, the foot, and the wall's ends stay solid, and every hole has a pointed roof so it prints without bridging. Short walls stay solid.

fields.label: Wide-face coverage
fields.help: How densely to line a WIDE overhang face with fins. The middle is the anti-sag default; drag LEFT for fewer fins (a small part can go down to one — the readout warns if a broad face then risks sagging), RIGHT for more support. Narrow parts are unaffected.

fields.label: Plate only
fields.help: Stand every support on the build plate, never on the part itself. An overhang with part under it is left unsupported, and the readout says how many.

fields.label: Separate walls
fields.help: Keep Full coverage fill walls from crossing other walls or sharing their bases: a resin print cures joined walls into one block that won't break away. Auto turns it on for Vertical (resin) tines and off for Horizontal (FDM), as the site does. Can leave more overhang unsupported; thin ties between tall walls stay, since they snap.

fields.label: Long walls
fields.help: Full coverage lays rows of long walls along the part's length first, the way you'd draw them by hand, then fills what they miss. Holds more of the overhang and uses more plastic. Untick for short walls under each overhang patch.

fields.label: Material
fields.help: The filament you print the supports in, for the weight under Support plastic.

fields.label: Bare beyond
fields.help: Overhangs further than this from a fin, or from the part itself, are shown bright red: they'd sag or fail. Bridging over a few mm works; over 5 mm usually droops.
